               …

faqs.a:
(a)
It shall be unlawful for any person to park, stand, or stop a motor vehicle upon any
               private parking lot or other private property within the city without the consent
               of the owner or the tenant or person in lawful possession or control of the private
               parking lot or private property.
(b)
Where the owner, tenant, or person in lawful control of private property places or
               posts a sign limiting, regulating, or restricting the parking, standing, or stopping
               of motor vehicles parked or left on the property, or prohibiting the parking, standing,
               or stopping of motor vehicles parked or left on the property, a motor vehicle parked
               or left on the property contrary to such regulations or prohibitions shall be deemed
               to have been parked or left without authority or consent.
(c)
No parking citation or summons shall be issued for any violation of this section,
               unless it is issued at the request of the owner, tenant, or person in lawful possession
               or control of the private parking lot or private property within or upon which the
               violation of this section alleged to have occurred. The person requesting the issuance
               of the citation or summons shall provide to the parking enforcement officer his or
               her name, address, and telephone number, and must agree to provide relevant information
               as needed.
(d)
Whenever the owner, tenant, or person in lawful possession or control of the private
               property finds a motor vehicle parked thereon without his or her consent, such owner,
               tenant, or person in lawful possession or control shall have the authority to have
               such motor vehicle towed in accordance with this section and at his or her expense.
(i)
No city employee or designee may authorize the tow or removal of a motor vehicle from
               a private parking lot or other private property pursuant to this section.
Exception: A police officer, or any employee of the city or other person designated
               by the chief of police to issue parking citations may authorize the tow or removal
               of a motor vehicle from a private parking lot that is either leased by the city for
               use as a private parking lot, or that is otherwise subject to a written agreement
               with the city that allows for the use of private property for public parking purposes,
               so long as the lease or other written agreement allows for such tows.
(e)
In the event the owner, tenant, or person in lawful possession or control of a private
               parking lot or private property has a motor vehicle towed in accordance with this
               section, he or she shall immediately notify the police department of such tow and
               indicate the name of the towing company that towed the vehicle, as well as the location
               of the lot to which the vehicle was towed.
(f)
Any sign posted pursuant to this section must indicate, in lettering not less than
               two inches high, the limitation, restriction, or prohibition on parking, standing,
               or stopping, and must be located and posted in such a manner as to be seen by an ordinarily
               observant person.
(
Ord. No. 4561, § 2, 8-29-2016
)
